paragraphs: My name is Lily, and I am ten years old. On Saturday, I came home at noon. There was a note on the fridge. It said, "Lily, I am at Grandma's in Green Hill. Back at six o'clock. Dad is in the garden. Love, Mom." I read the note two times, and I smiled. Mia and I wanted to meet at four o'clock at the park gate.

Dad came into the kitchen with his phone. "A message for you," he said. It said, "Hello, this is Mia's mom. Mia has a pain in her stomach, but she is OK. My husband will take her to the park tomorrow morning at ten o'clock. She says sorry." "Have you ever had a stomachache?" asked Dad. "Yes, after too much ice cream," I said. I wrote back, "Thank you! Get well soon, Mia."

On Sunday, Mia and her dad came to the park gate at ten o'clock. Mia was well again, and she looked happy. She held a small bike pump. "Thank you for your message," she said. "I have a million thanks for you!" We laughed a lot. Then we played on the grass near the pond until noon.

On Monday, Teacher Kim gave us a note. It said, "Write your name and your surname on the form. Bring it on Wednesday." I searched my bag, but the form was not there. It was in my pocket! "You have a million things in your bag," said Mia. I wrote my name and my surname. A short note gives the key facts: who, when, and where.
text.summary: Lily reads three short notes in three days. A note on the fridge, a message from Mia's mom, and a note from Teacher Kim tell her when and where.
